regime_context: US thematic leadership is concentrated in semis/AI-infra: AI Infrastructure (rank 1, eligible, trend-gate on), with WFE, Memory/HBM and Cybersecurity eligible directly behind. The absolute-trend gate HELPED historically (gate_helps=true), so trend discipline is credible for downside control, but cross-sectional momentum is rank-IC ~0 and rotation timing is display-only — ranking is a focus/downsize lens, not a return view. Rotation breadth is 'narrowing' (0.43 of themes eligible), and there is no one-narrative dominance.
emerging_watch: Watching whether 'AI Infrastructure' leadership (rank 1, durability_bar 0.73) hands off to 'AI Software & Platforms' (rank 21, score 0.09, eligible, hurst='trend', breadth 0.647 but crowding_z 0.78 and non-negative score). The observable that retires this watch is a confirmed two-week period where the AI Software proxy advances into the top-8 eligible ranks while AI Infra's durability_bar drops below 0.6 — until then this is a display-only hypothesis, not a call.

theses.subject: Memory, HBM & Storage
theses.thesis: Among the top AI/semis cluster, Memory/HBM is the only leader riding a clean 'trend' hurst_tag (vs 'mixed' for AI Infra and WFE), is eligible under the validated absolute-trend gate, and is NOT crowded (z=0.22) despite sitting at rank 3 — so it gets the trend-discipline downside protection without the crowding sizing caution that applies to WFE (z=1.01) and Cybersecurity (z=1.91). This is a relative-preference lean within the dominant cluster, not a standalone alpha claim.
evidence: hurst_tag='trend' vs 'mixed' for the top-2 themes — cleaner trend health
theses.dissent: Breadth is only 0.5 (half as wide as WFE at 0.938), so the trend may be carried by few names and vulnerable to a single-stock shock; the HBM supply story is well-known and the trend tag is coincident, not predictive.

falsifier.text: SMH lags SPY by 5% before the 20-day check-by date

theses.subject: Semiconductor Equipment (WFE)
theses.thesis: WFE is rank 2, eligible, and trend-gated, BUT its crowding flag (z=1.01, crowded=true) is exactly the documented sizing caution — and with three of the top five themes proxying to SMH (AI Infra, WFE, Memory, AI Semiconductors), single-proxy risk concentration is high. The guardrails explicitly forbid fading on crowding, so this is a mild relative AVOIDANCE under the same SMH umbrella where Memory offers comparable exposure with a cleaner trend and no crowding flag.
evidence: etf_proxy SMH shared with 3 other top-5 themes — concentration risk
hurst_tag='mixed' — less clean trend than Memory
theses.dissent: WFE has the widest breadth (0.938) and the strongest score after AI Infra; crowded leadership is often the most durable (reflexivity), and avoiding it within SMH gives only marginal differentiation since Memory and AI Semiconductors share the same proxy.

falsifier.text: SMH outperforms SPY by 5% while Memory/HBM shows no relative advantage over WFE inside SMH before the check-by date

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Cybersecurity is rank 4, eligible, with trend='trend' and perfect breadth (1.0) — the best trend-health in the whole eligible set — but crowding_z=1.91 is the most extreme flag in the top ranks. Per guardrails, crowding is NEVER a fade/short, only a size-down caution; combined with the fact that its proxy (CIBR) is a single-theme ETF and the rotation breadth is 'narrowing,' this is a lower-confidence avoid relative to the semis complex, not a bet against it.
evidence: crowding_z=1.91, crowded=true — highest flag in top ranks
hurst_tag='trend', breadth=1.0 — strong trend but fully picked-over
theses.dissent: The strongest breadth-cohesion (1.0) and a clean trend tag argue the theme is genuinely leading, and extreme crowding in a durable trend often persists; avoiding it forfeits a healthy-trend leg for a caution signal that carries no validated forward edge.

falsifier.text: CIBR outperforms SPY by 5% before the check-by date without a drawdown below its 20-day trend

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
